pr_title: Armclang / armlink support in Zephyr - Zephyr CMake linker functions
pr_body:
This is the initial support for Zephyr CMake linker functions.

Using CMake for linker script generations allows us to specify memory regions, linker sections, linker symbols in a common way using CMake functions, and then generate toolchain specific linker scripts / scatter files.

This allows users to only write things once and avoid linker scripts to get out of sync when only a single script (for example ld script) is updated, but not other linker scripts.

Besides a unifies Linker script language, another advantage of using CMake is that users can add new sections in their application CMakeLists.txt file.

Using CMake, a user can now write:
```
zephyr_linker_memory(NAME FOO FLAGS rx START 0x40000000 SIZE 1k)
zephyr_linker_section(NAME bar LMA FOO)
zephyr_linker_section_configure(SECTION bar INPUT baz KEEP)
```

and this can even be done in the app CMakeLists.txt file, like:
```
find_package(Zephyr REQUIRED)

target_sources(app PRIVATE baz.c)

zephyr_linker_memory(NAME FOO FLAGS rx START 0x40000000 SIZE 1k)
zephyr_linker_section(NAME bar LMA FOO)
zephyr_linker_section_configure(SECTION bar INPUT baz KEEP)
```

This will create a memory region named `FOO`, with a section `bar` where the input section `baz` will be placed with the KEEP flag.

Also it is possible to describe a new section in CMake together with the library as:
```
zephyr_library_named(pinmux)
zephyr_library_sources(pinmux.c)
zephyr_linker_section(NAME .pinmux GROUP ROM_REGION)
or
zephyr_linker_section(NAME .pinmux LMA ROM)
```

With this PR, the arm architecture has been ported to the new Zephyr CMake linker generator.

When building with armclang, the new linker generator is always used.
When building with `zephyr` or `gnuarmemb`, the old system will be used, and the new linker generator must be manually selected using: ` -DCONFIG_CMAKE_LINKER_GENERATOR=y` (or by using menuconfig).

To build using `armclang` set the toolchain to armclang and the path to the toolchain.
```
export ZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT=armclang
export ARMCLANG_TOOLCHAIN_PATH=/opt/armds-2020-1/sw/ARMCompiler6.15/
```

Building `hello_world` for `qemu_cortex_m3` using armclang / armlink:
```
$ cmake -GNinja -DBOARD=qemu_cortex_m3 -Bbuild_qemu samples/hello_world/
...
-- The C compiler identification is ARMClang 6.15.2
-- The CXX compiler identification is ARMClang 6.15.2
-- The ASM compiler identification is ARMClang
...
$ ninja -Cbuild_qemu run
[116/117] To exit from QEMU enter: 'CTRL+a, x'[QEMU] CPU: cortex-m3
qemu-system-arm: warning: nic stellaris_enet.0 has no peer
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v2.6.0-69-gcfa5059ceaeb  ***
Hello World! qemu_cortex_m3
```

and for `nrf52840dk_nrf52840`:
```
$ cmake -GNinja -DBOARD=nrf52840dk_nrf52840 -Bbuild samples/hello_world/
...
$ ninja -Cbuild run
$ ninja -Cbuild flash
...
...
-- runners.nrfjprog: Board with serial number 683845540 flashed successfully.
```
Open minicom and see the console output:
```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v2.6.0-69-gcfa5059ceaeb  ***
Hello World! nrf52840dk_nrf52840

```

Building with Zephyr toolchain using new linker generator:
```
$ export ZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT=zephyr
$ cmake -GNinja -DBOARD=qemu_cortex_m3 -Bbuild_qemu samples/hello_world/ 
 -DCONFIG_CMAKE_LINKER_GENERATOR=y
....
$ ninja -Cbuild_qemu run
[124/125] To exit from QEMU enter: 'CTRL+a, x'[QEMU] CPU: cortex-m3
qemu-system-arm: warning: nic stellaris_enet.0 has no peer
Timer with period zero, disabling
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v2.6.0-69-gcfa5059ceaeb  ***
Hello World! qemu_cortex_m3
```

ToDo:
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Kconfig setting for linker script generator
- [x] Memory sections from Device Tree
- [x] Linker groups / regions
- [ ] Userspace support
- [x] Linker symbols for groups
- [x] offset on section configure

Additional notes:
- CMake v3.18 or higher required, see #37575
- ~Issues seen when using `make`, so for time being, please use `ninja`~ CMake 3.21 with make is supported. Older CMake with make will issue a error message, see: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/d72ec887cdc51a8b5958756888b69f608fd1245b
- Warnings will be seen during linking. Those warnings will be cleaned up before going into mergable PR state.
- In general, memory regions should be defined using devicetree, and then Zephyr CMake linker template will create corresponding memory regions in the linker script, see #37624

The cleanup commit series can be found here as independent PR:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/37938

Fixes #33435

@tejlmand 

I wonder if this might tie in with #37123 (macos native_posix support).

The major issue with macos is that the Mach-O binary file format only supports section names 1 <= n <= 16 chars in length, and we generate a number of linker-defined sections that exceed that size.

One possible solution for that would be some kind of mapping for section names. I'll be looking at other solutions as well. Currently macos support is very brute force.

> @cfriedt I don't think so. This PR has nothing to do with Mach-O format or even Clang in general.

@stephanosio for context, I suggested that @cfriedt look at this PR because of commits like https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/36140/commits/5bf4e11e84650641eb6349e0e79491f33af2d76a. The problem on Mach-O is that section names can only be 16 characters long, so many existing zephyr linker script sections used for ELF which are longer than that won't fit. The abstraction layer between 'zephyr' symbols and 'linker' symbols being added here seemed potentially relevant.

> The major issue with macos is that the Mach-O binary file format only supports section names 1 <= n <= 16 chars in length, and we generate a number of linker-defined sections that exceed that size.
> 
> One possible solution for that would be some kind of mapping for section names. I'll be looking at other solutions as well. Currently macos support is very brute force.

@cfriedt Thanks for pointing my attention to this issue.
This for sure is something we should be able to handle in the linker script generator.
In code we rely on the linker script defined symbols, so we should be able to truncated the section names to <16 when building on macos, for native posix.

Will keep that in mind and probably ask for your review when this PR is out of draft, to get feedback on the macos part :wink:

An update has been posted.

This update contains:
- complete rewrite of scatter_script.cmake
- complete rewrite of ld_script.cmake
- Introduction of linker_script_common.cmake which are shared among linker script generators
- group feature added which means that multiple sections can be added to a group to ensure they are placed together.
  - This includes linker symbols defined for the start and end of such groups, `__<group>_start` and `__<group>_end`, for example `__rom_region_start` and `__rom_region_end` will be defined for the group `rom_region`.
  - Groups can be placed inside another group, for example:
    ```
    zephyr_linker_group(NAME ROM_REGION LMA FLASH)
    zephyr_linker_group(NAME TEXT_REGION GROUP ROM_REGION)
    ```
    resulting in symbols and location like:
    ```
    __rom_region_start;
    __text_region_start;
    __text_region_end;
    __rom_region_end;
    ```
- memory sections from devicetree
- more cleanup 

Also addressed:
> But common-rom.ld doesn't define a __rom_start_start symbol at the beginning, so this looks like it's now pointing to the wrong thing. 

With group feature in place, this should now be correct.

See diff, before rebase: 
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/compare/3191ee9dec1884a874199fb682eace4125bf3082..d563547027fa04021b454b15380e0d821e577494

The ARMClang / scatter file is now considered ready for review.

Documentation and ~Kconfig~ (Done) will follow shortly, but support for ARMClang is ready.

Note: CMake 3.20 with Ninja is recommended, if using Make, then CMake 3.21 must be used.

Currently Qemu for cortex-m and nRF52840dk targets has been used for building, flashing, and running.

I would like to discuss the steps required to merge this into main, along with the maintenance associated with it if `CONFIG_CMAKE_LINKER_GENERATOR` is set to `n` by default. This has nothing to do with armclang itself, it's about switching to the new CMake-based linker script generation even for GCC.

Currently `CONFIG_CMAKE_LINKER_GENERATOR`  only works on Arm, because the non-common linker scripts for non-Arm have not been ported yet. The `common-ram` and `common-rom` ones have been ported.

The referenced problem with NXP HAL is because we don't have the DefaultISR defined anywhere. With the NXP SDK, this is a "weak" symbol that is defined in our startup code. This was added to our codebase a while back to deal with a code size issue. Apparently, the armclang tool chain has a quirky behavior with pointers like this that eventually get set within a function. If that function is not referenced by the rest of the code, tool chains like GCC will properly prune that function from the final image. The armclang though does not. Something to do with a pointer that is initially pointing to a NULL.

> dev-review (Aug 19, 2021):
> ...
> 
>     * which libc are we getting?  (needs some verification, minlibc v arm-libc)

A small update on this particular item.
The arm linker will per default link to the ARM Standard C library, but that library does not contain all APIs Zephyr requires example, it only has `strlen`, not `strnlen`, secondly, the `errno.h` is more limited than what Zephyr expects.
That was the reason why minimal libc was still being linked. So some work is needed to carve out only the parts of minimal libc not provided by ARM Standard C lib, and required by Zephyr.

It is possible to disable linking with the ARM Standard library completely, by using the `-nostdlib`, `-nostdlibinc` and `-fno-built` option on the compiler, and during linking, the `--no_scanlib`.

Now, doing so all ARM C lib is disabled, including the low-level part with `__aeabi_X` implementations. (In GCC, this is provided in libgcc.a).
So it's not possible to then simply disable ARM C standard lib completely and link with Zephyr internal minimal libc or newlib, cause both of those libs relies on the low-level libgcc. (We could probably link manual to libgcc also, but then the point of using armclang kind of vanishes)

So currently we need to linking to a reduced minimal libc to be able to also link the features from Zephyr's minimal libc that is not available in ARM Standard C.

issue_context.title: armclang / armlinker
issue_context.body:
Feature:
Support for armclang / armlinker in Zephyr

Required:
Compiler infrastructure is in place and support for Vanilla clang on Linux works.
More work is needed for Windows, wrt. generated dependency files containg `\` in path which is later interpreted as escaped characters and thus results in CMake endless looping.

As part of this work, support for armlinker must be in place.
This work should result in better abstractions of linker description.

review_comments:
`__stdout_hook` is not used anywhere.

`libc-hooks.c` is supposed to override, for instance, `write()` so that the functions like `printf()` (which internally should call `write()` or something like that) print to the console through `_stdout_hook()`.

Though, I am ok with leaving this as is for now and adding the console I/O support as a future enhancement.

hmm, seems you're right.
I thought I had only added functions when I noticed they were needed, so right now I'm unsure how this got in.

Will keep until i'm confident it can be removed.
Thanks for spotting :+1:
